neighbours.label: The verb 'pick' (picked, picks, picking, pick), with or without 'up', as in picked up by the media or picked a dress, vs other verbs of taking or choosing in the same frame
fire: The puppy picks up every sock it finds and hides it under the sofa.
Her short video was picked up by a popular morning show the next day.
He picked the blue bicycle because it was the lightest in the shop.
On Saturdays the children go picking strawberries at the farm.
Once the story was picked up by the wire services, it spread worldwide.
She always picks the seat nearest the window on long flights.
Volunteers spent the morning picking litter off the beach.
After a slow spring, sales picked up sharply in the summer months.
quiet: The puppy steals every sock it finds and hides it under the sofa.
Her short video was shown on a popular morning show the next day.
He chose the blue bicycle because it was the lightest in the shop.
On Saturdays the children go looking for strawberries at the farm.
Once the story was carried by the wire services, it spread worldwide.
She always books the seat nearest the window on long flights.
Volunteers spent the morning clearing litter off the beach.
After a slow spring, sales rose sharply in the summer months.

predictions: ' picked'/' picks'/' picking' reach 0.4-0.9; 'chose', 'grabbed', 'lifted', 'collected' in the same frames stay under 0.15.
notes: Card: ' picked' x10, ' pick' x8, ' picks' x4, ' taken' x2 (taken up), all before 'up'; the - pole promotes 'up'. Probe: 'picked up by several national newspapers' 0.825, 'picks up the tennis ball' 0.480, 'picked her keys up' 0.507, 'picked the red dress' 0.507 (no 'up'), 'taken up by the roots' 0.504, 'economy picked up' 0.247; 'drops the ball' 0.082, 'denied by' 0.049. 'picked' fires without 'up', so the label is the verb, not the particle.
